decisions.original_markdown: Dedicated model-organism infrastructures show what good stewardship looks like — the Rat Genome Database curates multi-species genomic and phenotype data explicitly to fulfil FAIR, {cite:p}`Vedi2023` and the European Mouse Mutant Archive established ten Quality Principles to standardize the scientific evaluation of cryopreserved rodent disease models {cite:p}`Ehlich2025` — but these are islands, and metadata tooling for experimental in vivo work, such as the ISA framework in environmental-health science, is still being retrofitted onto fields that never captured it natively. {cite:p}`Nault2023`
decisions.replacement_markdown: The Rat Genome Database describes its curated resource as advancing data reproducibility and fulfilling FAIR principles. {cite:p}`Vedi2023` INFRAFRONTIER/EMMA has developed ten Quality Principles tailored to cryopreserved rodent mutant strains. {cite:p}`Ehlich2025` Environmental-health metadata initiatives include development of the ISA framework and CEDAR. {cite:p}`Nault2023`

decisions.original_markdown: In animal work the picture repeats: orthodontic studies scored a mean of 57.9 on ARRIVE years after its release; {cite:p}`Flitti2024` ARRIVE 2.0 audits of Parkinson's and cardiovascular models found only about two-fifths of items well reported and no study reporting sample-size calculations, adverse events, or humane endpoints; {cite:p}`Park2025, Lin2024` a nationwide before-and-after comparison found explicit 3Rs reporting crept from 0% to just 3.2% across a decade; {cite:p}`Kousholt2023` and kidney, liver-regeneration, veterinary-emergency, traditional-medicine, and bone-defect surveys converge on the same picture of persistent, barely-moving deficits in randomisation, blinding, sample-size justification, and control design. {cite:p}`Chatzimanouil2018, Tihanyi2019, Bergen2023, Feng2024, Reimann2026, Yi2026, Majdi2025, Laing2026`

claims.claim_text: An audit of orthodontic animal studies reported a mean ARRIVE score of 57.9.
In a Parkinson's-disease animal-model review, 15 of 38 ARRIVE 2.0 items had compliance levels of 80–100%.
A broader audit of interventional animal experiments found significant post-ARRIVE improvement in 15 of 38 reporting subitems.
A nationwide comparison found explicit 3Rs reporting increased from zero publications in 2009 to 3.2% in 2018.

Manual audits across several animal-research domains continue to report deficits in randomisation, sample-size justification, control design, or related safeguards; however, the magnitude and direction of change vary by field and measurement method.

claim_scope.methodological: manual domain audits compared with automated reporting metrics

claims.independence_basis: Human review retained seven domain-specific audits from distinct bibliography author groups; shared authors are still conservatively grouped by the migration script.

passages.text: Between 1997 and 2020 (where data were readily available in our data set), rigor and transparency measures showed general improvement (RTI 2.29 to 4.13), suggesting that authors are taking the need for improved reporting seriously.

additional_citation_contexts.notes: Contrasting whole-literature automated index retained during approved human review to qualify the domain-specific manual-audit trend.

conflicts.notes: Whole-literature automated scoring detects improvement while domain-specific manual audits report persistent item-level deficits; the divergence is method- and field-dependent.
